;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]], [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Turkey|Turkish]]-backed rebels launch an offensive in the [[Idlib Governorate]] against [[government of Syria|government]] forces. A Russian  air strike kills two [[Turkish Land Forces|Turkish soldiers]] and injures five others, while Turkey says a retaliatory strike killed 50 [[Syrian Army|Syrian troops]]. Several tanks and armoured personnel carriers are destroyed near the village of [[Nayrab, Idlib|Nayrab]]. [https://www.news.com.au/world/breaking-news/turkey-says-strike-kills-50-syrian-forces/news-story/d36e8d6ddb62c9d49308a80ce6781c8d (News AU)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/fighting-rages-northwest-syria-turkish-troops-killed-200220131908647.html (Al Jazeera)]
**Turkey formally requests the deployment of [[MIM-104 Patriot|Patriot]] [[surface-to-air missile]] systems by its [[NATO]] ally [[United States]] on the [[Syria–Turkey border]] to deter Syrian and [[Russia]]n air strikes on its troops. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/02/20/turkey-asks-us-patriot-missiles-two-turkish-soldiers-killed/ (''The Telegraph'')] [https://www.almasdarnews.com/article/turkey-requests-us-patriot-missile-system-to-stop-russia-in-idlib-report/ (''Al Masdar News'')]

;Art and culture
*An 18th-century [[Ethiopia]]n ceremonial crown, one of the 20 in existence, is returned to [[Prime Minister of Ethiopia|Prime Minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]]. It was discovered in the [[Netherlands]] in 1998, and was held by Dutch authorities until now so it could be returned when the country was more politically stable. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-51571409 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Morgan Stanley]] purchases [[Electronic trading platform|electronic trading]] firm [[E-Trade]] for [[U.S. dollar|US$]]13 billion, in the largest banking deal since the [[Financial crisis of 2007–08|2008 financial crisis]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2020/feb/20/morgan-stanley-buys-e-trade-13bn (''The Guardian'')]

**A [[New South Wales XPT|XPT train]] derails in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], [[Australia]], killing two people. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2020/feb/20/sydney-to-melbourne-xpt-train-derails-in-victoria (''The Guardian'')]
*A 200-car pileup in [[La Prairie, Quebec|La Prairie]], [[Quebec]], [[Canada]], kills two people and injures 69 others. [https://www.news.com.au/world/north-america/two-people-killed-in-horror-200car-pileup-on-canadian-highway/news-story/17ff2110a61e5151501d9d4be08044fc (News AU)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
***South Korea reports its first death from [[COVID-19]]. [https://sputniknews.com/asia/202002201078358360-south-korea-reports-its-first-death-from-coronavirus/ (Sputnik)]
**Two [[Japanese people|Japanese]] passengers who were on board of the ''[[Diamond Princess (ship)|Diamond Princess]]'' [[cruise ship]] have died from the disease. Both, a man and a woman in their 80s, had underlying health conditions. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-51568496 (BBC News)]
**Australia extends its ban on travel from [[China]] for the fourth week in a row. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/20/australia-extends-coronavirus-ban-on-travel-from-china-into-fourth-week (''The Guardian'')]

;International relations
*''[[The Guardian]]'' reveals that [[Australia]]n ambassador to [[Myanmar]] Andrea Faulkner met with [[Commander-in-chief]] of the [[Tatmadaw|Burmese Armed Forces]] [[Min Aung Hlaing]] last month to discuss improving relations between the two nations and possibly training Hlaing's officers in Australia, among others. [[Human Rights Watch]] criticized this meeting as enabling Hlaing's [[Persecution of Muslims in Myanmar#Human rights violations against Rohingya|genocide]] against the [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/21/australian-ambassador-meets-with-myanmar-military-chief-accused-of-rohingya-genocide (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*Weeks after the First Lady of [[Lesotho]] [[Maesiah Thabane]] was arrested and charged with the killing of former First Lady [[Lipolelo Thabane]], it is announced that current [[Prime Minister of Lesotho]] [[Tom Thabane]] will also be charged with the murder in the upcoming hours. He also announced he will be stepping down at the end of July citing old age. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lesotho-politics/lesothos-prime-minister-to-be-charged-with-murdering-wife-police-idUSKBN20E1I4 (Reuters)]
* [[Criminal charges brought in the Mueller special counsel investigation]]
** [[U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia]] Judge [[Amy Berman Jackson]] sentences [[Roger Stone]], long-time adviser and ally to the [[President of the United States]] [[Donald Trump]], to 40 months in federal prison for seven charges of obstruction, lying to Congress and [[witness tampering]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/politics/live-news/roger-stone-sentencing/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-51580160 (BBC News)]
*[[Attorney General of New Mexico|New Mexican Attorney General]] [[Hector Balderas]] sues [[Google]] for allegedly collecting private information of [[New Mexico|the state]]'s schoolchildren without parental consent. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-alphabet-lawsuit/new-mexico-ag-sues-google-for-collecting-personal-data-of-school-children-idUSKBN20E2PA?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Dominican Republic municipal elections]]
**Protests happen in major [[Dominican Republic]] cities over the [[2020 Dominican Republic general election|election]] problems. [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/local/2020/02/20/electoral-fiasco-protests-spread-to-major-cities/ (''Dominican Today'')]
**Col. Ramón A. Guzmán and Claro telecom technician Manuel Antonio Regalado were arrested for the election sabotage. [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/local/2020/02/20/two-arrests-in-dominican-republic-election-sabotage/ (''Dominican Today'')]
*[[President of South Sudan|South Sudanese President]] [[Salva Kiir Mayardit]] and [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement-in-Opposition|SPLM-IO]] leader [[Riek Machar]] agree to form a unity government by Saturday, in a major step to end the [[South Sudanese Civil War]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/sudan-president-rebel-leader-agrees-form-unity-government-200220121647669.html (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[California State Legislature]] unanimously passes a resolution apologizing for [[California|the state]]'s role in  [[Internment of Japanese-Americans|interning Japanese-Americans]] during [[World War II]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/feb/20/california-japanese-internment-camps-apology (''The Guardian'')]
*Aftermath of the [[2020 Irish general election]]
**The [[Members of the 33rd Dáil|33rd]] [[Dáil Éireann]] meets for the election of the [[Taoiseach]] (head of government) and [[Ceann Comhairle]] (speaker of parliament).
**[[Seán Ó Fearghaíl]] of [[Fianna Fáil]] is re-elected as [[Ceann Comhairle]]. No candidate for Taoiseach attains the 80 votes required to form a government. The Dáil adjourns until March 5. [https://www.rte.ie/news/politics/2020/0220/1116469-ireland-politics/ ''(RTÉ)'']
**Incumbent Taoiseach [[Leo Varadkar]] offers his resignation to [[President of Ireland|President]] [[Michael D. Higgins]], but will remain as Taoiseach in a caretaker capacity until the formation of a new government. [https://news.sky.com/story/ireland-taoiseach-leo-varadkar-resigns-after-inconclusive-election-result-11939114 (Sky News)]
